work.note: Famosa corrida de cavalos de Melbourne, na Austrália, realizada desde 1861 na primeira terça-feira de novembro. Muita gente acompanha a prova em festas e pela TV. “The cup was won by a horse” é uma frase típica do passivo. A cena desta aula é original; não reproduz a obra.

facts.label: Passivo: was delivered, was sent
facts.sub: Afirmativa: The package was delivered. Pergunta: Was it returned? Negativa: It wasn’t delivered. Use by para dizer quem: It was sent by my sister.

facts.label: Passivo no passado
facts.sub: Use was/were + particípio para dizer o que aconteceu com algo: The package was delivered. O foco está no pacote, e quem entregou fica em segundo plano.

facts.label: Por quem
facts.sub: Use by para dizer quem fez: It was sent by my sister. Se não importa quem, deixe sem by: The letter was returned. Em avisos do correio, o agente quase nunca aparece.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “The package was delivered” is a past passive.
We say “The package delivered on Monday.”
“It was sent by my sister” is correct.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: “The package was delivered” is a past passive. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “The package delivered on Monday.” → Falso (We say was delivered.)
“It was sent by my sister” is correct. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: We can leave out by + person.

pages.instruction: Mais uma rodada: decida e explique.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: With letters (plural), we say “was returned”. → Falso (We say were returned.)
We can leave out by + person. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: The post office · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot Friday morning in Melbourne. Ben walks into the post office with a card in his hand. There is a short line in front of the counter. Lou works behind the counter. She knows most of the customers. Ben is waiting for a package from Brazil.

“Good morning, Ben. Your package was delivered here on Monday.” says Lou. “Great! It was sent by my sister in Brazil two weeks ago.” says Ben. “Two weeks! It was delayed at the airport for some days.” says Lou.
